title: Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse
title_zh: T细胞耗竭的蛋白组图谱揭示蛋白稳态崩溃
abstract: T cell exhaustion limits the success of cancer immunotherapies, yet the proteomic changes underlying this dysfunctional state remain poorly understood. We integrated transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, turnover proteomics, and ubiquitin proteomics to construct a multi-omic atlas of T cell exhaustion. These studies identified pathways regulated through transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, including degradative and nondegradative ubiquitin modifications, and uncovered widespread changes in proteostasis, metabolism, and DNA repair. Major shifts were revealed in the ubiquitin-proteasome system, as differential expression of E3 ubiquitin ligases correlates with immunotherapy outcomes. These findings position the collapse of proteostasis as a central, underappreciated feature of T cell exhaustion and reveal opportunities to restore T cell function. We demonstrate that overexpression of the E3 ligase RNF166 enhances T cell persistence in vitro and in vivo. This work defines proteome-turnover dynamics as a critical regulatory layer in progressive T cell dysfunction, with broad implications for advancing cancer immunotherapy through manipulation of E3 ligases.
abstract_zh: T细胞耗竭限制了癌症免疫治疗的成功，但导致这一功能失调状态的蛋白组变化仍不清楚。我们整合转录组学、定量蛋白组学、蛋白质周转蛋白组学和泛素蛋白组学，构建了T细胞耗竭的多组学图谱。研究发现，转录和翻译后机制调控的通路包括降解性和非降解性泛素修饰，并揭示了蛋白稳态、代谢和DNA修复的广泛变化。泛素-蛋白酶体系统出现显著转变，E3泛素连接酶的差异表达与免疫治疗结果相关。结果表明，蛋白稳态崩溃是T细胞耗竭的核心、被低估的特征，并为恢复T细胞功能提供了机会。我们证明，E3连接酶RNF166的过表达可增强T细胞在体内外的持久性。此工作将蛋白质周转动力学定义为进展性T细胞功能障碍的关键调控层，对通过操纵E3连接酶推进癌症免疫治疗具有广泛意义。
